title: Lampang with Kids: 3-Day Family Itinerary | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A relaxed 3-day, 2-night Lampang family itinerary in northern Thailand: bathe with elephants, ride a horse-drawn carriage, soak in Chae Son hot springs, paint a rooster bowl. Real timings and prices, easy travel days.
keywords: Lampang with kids, Lampang family itinerary, Thai Elephant Conservation Center, Lampang horse carriage, Chae Son hot springs
intro: Lampang is an easy city to bring kids to. Distances in town are short, traffic is light, and there are activities children actually enjoy — watching elephants bathe, riding a carriage to the clip-clop of horseshoes on the road, soaking in hot springs out in the forest, and painting a rooster bowl to take home. Here's a 3-day, 2-night plan that won't wear anyone out: it leaves room for little ones to nap and builds in real travel time for every leg.
chips: ♨️ Soak at Chae Son hot springs

blocks.html: First, the big picture. Lampang splits into two main zones for sightseeing: in town (horse carriages, Kad Kong Ta, the city temples, ceramic painting) and out of town, where you'll need a car — the Thai Elephant Conservation Center and Wat Phra That Lampang Luang to the south and west, and Chae Son National Park further out to the north, about an hour and a half away. This plan groups the nearby spots together on the same day so the kids aren't stuck in the car too long.

blocks.title: Before you go
blocks.html: Lampang has almost no public transport that's convenient for a family. Renting a car to drive yourself, or hiring a car with a driver, is the way to go — the big draws like the elephant center and Chae Son are out of town. If you're only doing the in-town spots, the horse carriages and local pickup taxis can cover it, but with small kids a private car is much easier.

blocks.text: Day 1 — In Town: Carriages, Ceramics, Kad Kong Ta

blocks.html: Keep the first day gentle so the kids can settle in. Stick to town, with short drives and easy parking, nothing too demanding. Save the evening for a stroll through Kad Kong Ta if it happens to fall on a Saturday or Sunday.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: In Town: Carriage, Ceramics, Walking Street

items.activity: Check in at your in-town hotel, drop your bags, and rest off the trip.
items.note: Pick a hotel in the town center near Ratsada Bridge — it makes getting anywhere easy.

items.activity: Take a short horse-carriage loop around town, starting from the rank in front of the old provincial hall, across Ratsada Bridge, past the old riverside buildings along the Wang River.
items.note: Short city loop 150 THB, longer loop 200 THB, or hire by the hour at 300 THB. The carriage rank runs 06:00–16:00. Kids usually get a kick out of the horseshoe sound.

items.activity: Lunch at a place in town — try khao soi or the kuaytiao kao lao (clear pork-blood noodle soup) that Lampang is known for.
items.note: Most in-town restaurants have high chairs and parking.

items.activity: Dhanabadee Ceramic Museum: learn the story behind Lampang's original rooster bowls, then let the kids paint a bowl or cup to take home.
items.note: Open daily 09:00–17:00. Admission for Thai adults 60 THB, students 30 THB. The painting workshop runs 60–300 THB depending on the size of the piece.

items.activity: Head back to the hotel and let the little ones grab an afternoon nap.
items.note: Build this break in — the kids will be in a much better mood come evening.

items.activity: Walk Kad Kong Ta, the riverside walking street along the Wang River: local street food, handmade toys, century-old shophouses.
items.note: Open Saturdays and Sundays only, 16:00–22:00. On a weekday, stroll along the Yang dam instead or find a dinner spot with a nice view.

blocks.title: Carriages with small kids
blocks.html: The carriages have no seatbelts, so a parent needs to stay right beside the child the whole time and hold on tight crossing the bridge. If your child is very young or nervous about the noise, start with a short loop to see how they handle it.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Thai Elephant Conservation Center + Wat Phra That Lampang Luang

blocks.html: This is the highlight day for the kids. The Thai Elephant Conservation Center is in Hang Chat district, about a 30-minute drive from town. Go a bit early to catch the morning elephant-bathing round and the show, then stop at Wat Phra That Lampang Luang in the afternoon since it's on the same route.

items.activity: Leave town for the Thai Elephant Conservation Center in Hang Chat district.
items.note: About 30 km, roughly 30 minutes.

items.activity: Arrive at the elephant center, walk the grounds, feed the elephants, and wait for the activity round.
items.note: Open daily 09:00–16:00. Elephant feeding is 50 THB a basket — kids love it.

items.activity: Watch the elephants bathe and play in the water at the morning round — the part kids enjoy most.
items.note: Bathing rounds are usually 10:45 and 13:15. Double-check on site, as times can shift with the season.

items.activity: Catch the elephant 'classroom' show — elephants painting and playing music.
items.note: Shows are usually 11:00 and 13:30. Show tickets are 200 THB for adults, 150 THB for children.

items.activity: Lunch at the center's restaurant, or drive out and find a place along the way.
items.note: There's a restaurant and a coffee shop inside the center.

items.activity: Drive to Wat Phra That Lampang Luang in Ko Kha district, an ancient Lanna wooden temple, and see the upside-down reflection of the chedi inside the viharn.
items.note: About 30–40 minutes from the elephant center. Dress modestly. The temple grounds are easy to walk and partly stroller-friendly.

items.activity: Head back into town, rest, and keep dinner simple near the hotel.
items.note: Lots of walking today, so the kids will tire quickly. Save some energy for tomorrow.

blocks.title: Choosing kid-friendly elephant activities
blocks.html: If you're worried about animal welfare or your kids are still small, just watching the elephants bathe and feeding them is plenty — no need to ride one. The kids will still have a great time, and it's safer.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Chae Son: Hot-Spring Soak and Onsen-Boiled Eggs

blocks.html: Spend the last day in nature at Chae Son National Park in Mueang Pan district, about an hour and a half from town. There are hot springs for boiling eggs, foot-soaking pools, and private mineral-bath rooms. Kids love boiling eggs in a basket. Set out a little early so there's plenty of time to play before the drive home.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: A Mineral Soak in the Forest

items.activity: Check out and drive to Chae Son National Park.
items.note: About 75 km, roughly 1.5 hours. The road climbs a little, so pack motion-sickness medicine for kids who get carsick easily.

items.activity: Arrive at Chae Son, buy eggs to boil in the hot spring — kids love waiting for them to cook.
items.note: Park entry is 40 THB for adults, 20 THB for children, and 30 THB for the car. Open 06:00–18:00.

items.activity: Soak your feet in the mineral pools, or book a private mineral-bath room for the family.
items.note: The hot springs bubble up from several small pools across an open plaza, with safe spots for kids to dip their feet.

items.activity: Lunch at the park restaurant, sitting beside the cool stream.
items.note: Shady and relaxed — good for letting the kids run around.

items.activity: Take a short walk to see Chae Son Waterfall and grab some photos before heading back.
items.note: The trail is short, but watch your footing near the falls — it gets slippery.

items.activity: Start the drive back, stopping for souvenirs along the way, such as khao taen (crispy rice cakes) or rooster bowls.
items.note: Allow for traffic heading back into town or on to the airport/train station.

blocks.text: What Kind of Stay Suits a Family

blocks.html: For a family with kids, stay in central Lampang near Ratsada Bridge or the Kad Kong Ta area — it balances travel to every zone, with restaurants and convenience stores close by, and the horse-carriage rank is right there too. Pick a room with an extra bed or a family room, and if there are several of you, a resort with space for the kids to run around beats a high-rise hotel.

items.name: Riverside Hotel in Town on the Wang River
items.blurb: Walk to Kad Kong Ta and the carriage rank, with an easy start for trips out to the elephant center or Chae Son. Good for families who'd rather not switch hotels.

items.name: Suburban Resort with Outdoor Space
items.blurb: A garden or pool for the kids, quieter, and a good fit if you have little ones who nap and want a more open setting.

blocks.text: Tips for an Easy, Fun Trip to Lampang with Kids

items: Group nearby spots on one day — the elephant center and Wat Phra That Lampang Luang are on the same route, so do them together and skip the back-and-forth.
Always start early — the morning elephant-bathing and show rounds are less crowded, the air is still cool, and the kids are in better spirits.
Leave room for naps — little ones need an afternoon break. This plan builds one in, so don't cram the day full.
Pack the essentials — hats, sunscreen, motion-sickness medicine, a towel for the hot-spring day, and non-slip shoes for the waterfall.
Kad Kong Ta is weekends only — line up your days. Come on a weekday and there's no walking street.

faq.q: How many days are ideal for visiting Lampang with kids?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is about right. Day one is a light tour of town to let the kids settle in, day two is the elephant center and Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, and the last day is the Chae Son hot springs. If you're really short on time, two days and one night still covers the town and the elephant center.

faq.q: What time are the elephant-bathing rounds at the Thai Elephant Conservation Center in Lampang?
faq.a: The elephants usually bathe and play in the water at 10:45 and 13:15, while the elephant 'classroom' show runs at 11:00 and 13:30. The center is open 09:00–16:00. Go in the morning to catch the first round and avoid the harsh sun — times can shift with the season, so check again on site.

faq.q: Is Chae Son doable with small kids?
faq.a: Yes, though the road climbs a little and it's about an hour and a half from town, so pack motion-sickness medicine for kids who get carsick easily. Boiling eggs in the hot spring and soaking their feet are big hits with kids. Entry is 40 THB for adults and 20 THB for children.

faq.q: Can you see in-town Lampang without your own car?
faq.a: In town, you can manage with the horse carriages and pickup taxis. But spots like the elephant center and Chae Son are out of town with no convenient public transport, so for a whole family, renting a car to drive yourself or hiring one with a driver is far more practical.

faq.q: How much does a Lampang horse carriage cost, and is it safe for kids?
faq.a: The short city loop is 150 THB, the longer loop 200 THB, or hire by the hour at 300 THB. The carriages have no seatbelts, so a parent needs to sit beside the child and hold on tight, especially crossing the bridge. If your child is very young, start with a short loop first.
